branches.title: How many comparisons does that take?
branches.source: Each match keeps only the smaller value because the larger one cannot be the overall minimum: we already know a value smaller than it. Advancing the smaller value ensures the overall minimum stays in the tournament.

anchor.question: How many comparisons does that take?
anchor.snapshot: A tournament tree finds the minimum of eight numbers by comparing pairs and advancing the smaller value through successive rounds. The larger value is discarded because it cannot be the overall minimum; advancing the smaller value keeps the overall minimum in contention. Finding the minimum takes seven comparisons total: four in the first round, two in the second, and one in the final. The learner now asks how many comparisons this takes.
